rules.statement: The plaintiff could not enforce a contract for a distillery license that was never applied for or accepted, even if the circular letter held out an inducement to form such a contract.
rules.supporting_quote: With regard to the second point, the contract to grant the distillery license for the purposes mentioned In the circular is a matter altogether apart from an ordinary application for a distiller's 434 license contemplated by the Ordinance and I do not think the Government can be heard to say that the only remedy, in case the Government refused to carry out the contract, was an appeal to itself. In my opinion, however, the appellant never applied for and was never willing to accept the license that he was entitled to under his contract, namely, a license trammelled with the condition that all arrack distilled should be used for the purposes of his own rents.

meta.parties: De Soysa v. The Attorney General
